INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #11
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which sentence has a plural noun? (1 mark)
   A. Mother buys three bananas.
   B. Mother buys a banana.
   C. Mother buys one mango.
   D. Mother buys sugar.

2. Why is neat handwriting important? (1 mark)
   A. It makes the book heavier
   B. It makes the pencil last longer
   C. It is only for teachers
   D. It helps the reader to understand the message

3. A sentence should end with a (1 mark)
   A. drawing
   B. capital letter
   C. full stop
   D. comma

4. A sentence should begin with (1 mark)
   A. a number
   B. a capital letter
   C. a small drawing
   D. a comma

5. Which game teaches that messages can change when passed on? (1 mark)
   A. Football
   B. Chinese whisper
   C. Skipping
   D. Hide and seek only

6. Which sentence uses a signal word for the last step? (1 mark)
   A. First, wait.
   B. Then, wait.
   C. Next, wait.
   D. Finally, wait until the rain stops.

7. A sentence always begins with (1 mark)
   A. a comma
   B. a capital letter
   C. a number
   D. a full stop

8. A comma is used to (1 mark)
   A. separate items in a list
   B. end a story
   C. begin a sentence
   D. show a question

9. In The road was congested and the matatu could not move, what does congested mean? (1 mark)
   A. Very clean
   B. Very crowded
   C. Very short
   D. Very wide

10. What do we do in a matching game with words? (1 mark)
   A. Draw a picture only
   B. Sing a song
   C. Match each word with its meaning
   D. Count the cards

11. What is the best way to check the order of your paragraph? (1 mark)
   A. Copy it
   B. Cover it
   C. Read it aloud
   D. Fold the page

12. What is a level reader? (1 mark)
   A. A book written for a particular reading level
   B. A tool for measuring floors
   C. A machine
   D. A type of dictionary

13. What is the subject of a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. The verb only
   B. What is said about it
   C. Who or what the sentence is about
   D. The full stop

14. Which preposition needs two things to make sense? (1 mark)
   A. on
   B. under
   C. in
   D. between

15. Which is a domestic animal? (1 mark)
   A. Zebra
   B. Goat
   C. Lion
   D. Elephant

16. Why record yourself reciting? (1 mark)
   A. To lose the poem
   B. To listen back and improve
   C. To stop practising
   D. To delete your voice

17. What is creative writing? (1 mark)
   A. Copying a text exactly
   B. Writing a list of names
   C. Writing only numbers
   D. Using imagination to write stories, poems and other pieces

18. What are peers? (1 mark)
   A. People of your own age or class
   B. Only teachers
   C. Only parents
   D. Animals

19. What is a polite way to disagree in a debate? (1 mark)
   A. Shut up
   B. You are wrong and silly
   C. Leave now
   D. I respectfully disagree

20. What is an interjection? (1 mark)
   A. A short word that shows a sudden feeling
   B. A word that joins sentences
   C. A word that names a thing
   D. A word that shows position

21. How should you start a new speaker's words in a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. On the same line as before
   B. On a new line
   C. At the end of the page
   D. Inside a bracket

22. What should you not do with an advert that asks for money from strangers? (1 mark)
   A. Read it carefully
   B. Ask an adult
   C. Send money without asking an adult
   D. Check the facts

23. What should you do before buying a product that an advert says is the best in the world? (1 mark)
   A. Buy it at once
   B. Check it and the price
   C. Send money to a stranger
   D. Believe everything

24. Where should your class keep collected forms? (1 mark)
   A. In the river
   B. Under a stone
   C. In the fire
   D. In a portfolio

25. What should you do when someone else is speaking? (1 mark)
   A. Leave
   B. Talk over them
   C. Draw
   D. Listen without interrupting

26. Which pair of verbs shows an action? (1 mark)
   A. table, chair
   B. vote, count
   C. is, are
   D. red, blue

27. What is rhythm? (1 mark)
   A. The beat or flow when a poem is read aloud
   B. The ink
   C. The title
   D. The page number

28. What should you add when a task is dangerous? (1 mark)
   A. A song
   B. A joke
   C. A warning
   D. A colour

29. What should each step in written instructions usually start with? (1 mark)
   A. A colour
   B. A number only
   C. A verb
   D. A name

30. Why should each step contain only one action? (1 mark)
   A. So it is clear and easy to follow
   B. To use fewer words
   C. To confuse readers
   D. To make it longer

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Complete each sentence with a suitable verb: (a) We ______ our hands before eating. (b) Please ______ the door. (3 marks)

32. Describe how you would scan a passage to find how much a box of mangoes costs. (4 marks)

33. Explain what a story setting is. (2 marks)

34. Write two compound sentences about shopping using so and but. (4 marks)

35. Explain why clear instructions are important when it rains. (3 marks)

36. Explain what the proverb Honesty is the best policy means. (2 marks)

37. Explain what a stanza is. (2 marks)

38. Correct this paragraph: it was a cold morning in nyeri the children wore sweaters scarves and socks (4 marks)

39. Explain how to work out the meaning of an unknown word using context. (4 marks)

40. Divide into subject and predicate: My brother saves coins. (2 marks)

41. Write a four-sentence paragraph on washing hands. Use first, next, then and finally. (4 marks)

42. Give three rules of good telephone manners. (3 marks)

43. List three steps for explaining a proverb. (3 marks)

44. Explain what the proverb Many hands make light work means. (2 marks)

45. List three ways of taking good care of a domestic animal. (3 marks)

46. Find the rhyming words in: Feed the hen at break of day, Give her water, let her play. (2 marks)

47. Give three parts of a news item. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #11 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Mother buys three bananas.
   Bananas is plural, and the number three shows there are more than one.

2. D — It helps the reader to understand the message
   A message is useful only if it can be read.

3. C — full stop
   A statement ends with a full stop.

4. B — a capital letter
   Every sentence starts with a capital letter.

5. B — Chinese whisper
   In Chinese whisper the message changes as it passes.

6. D — Finally, wait until the rain stops.
   Finally shows the last step.

7. B — a capital letter
   A capital letter shows the start of a sentence.

8. A — separate items in a list
   Commas separate list items and show short pauses.

9. B — Very crowded
   The matatu could not move because there was too much traffic.

10. C — Match each word with its meaning
   The game links words to meanings.

11. C — Read it aloud
   Reading aloud shows if the order makes sense.

12. A — A book written for a particular reading level
   Level readers match the skills of the pupils.

13. C — Who or what the sentence is about
   The subject is the topic of the sentence.

14. D — between
   Between means with something on each side.

15. B — Goat
   Goats are kept by people.

16. B — To listen back and improve
   Playback shows how to improve.

17. D — Using imagination to write stories, poems and other pieces
   Creative writing is imaginative.

18. A — People of your own age or class
   Peers are people like you in age or class.

19. D — I respectfully disagree
   Polite words show respect.

20. A — A short word that shows a sudden feeling
   Interjections show emotion.

21. B — On a new line
   A new line shows a new speaker.

22. C — Send money without asking an adult
   Never send money to strangers.

23. B — Check it and the price
   Adverts try to persuade so we check.

24. D — In a portfolio
   A portfolio keeps them organised.

25. D — Listen without interrupting
   Respectful listening is key.

26. B — vote, count
   Vote and count are actions.

27. A — The beat or flow when a poem is read aloud
   Rhythm is the pattern of sounds.

28. C — A warning
   Warnings keep people safe.

29. C — A verb
   Steps begin with action words.

30. A — So it is clear and easy to follow
   One action per step is clear.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: wash (or clean) and close (or shut)
   Working / marking points: One mark for each suitable verb and one mark for correct spelling.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Know that you are looking for the price, run your eyes over the text looking for numbers, stop at the number, read the sentence around it and check that it answers the question.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: The setting is the place and time where the story happens.
   Working / marking points: One mark for place and one for time.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: I had money, so I bought bread. I wanted a toy, but it was too costly.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct sentence and one for each correct comma.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Clear instructions tell people what to do to stay safe and dry, so they do not make mistakes or get hurt.
   Working / marking points: One mark for staying safe, one for avoiding mistakes, one for a clear link to rain.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: Telling the truth is always the wisest choice because it builds trust.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for the reason.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: A stanza is a group of lines in a poem, separated from the next group by a space.
   Working / marking points: One mark for group of lines and one for separation.

38. (4 marks)
   Answer: It was a cold morning in Nyeri. The children wore sweaters, scarves and socks.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four corrections: capitals at the start, Nyeri, the full stops and the commas.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Read the sentence with the word, look at nearby words for clues, guess a meaning, check that it makes sense in the sentence and confirm in a dictionary.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: Subject: My brother. Predicate: saves coins.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each part.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: First, wet your hands. Next, rub soap on them. Then rinse them. Finally, dry them with a clean cloth.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct step in order and sequence word.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Greet, give your name, speak clearly, do not interrupt, do not call late without a reason, say goodbye.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Say it slowly, picture what it shows, decide the lesson, think of a real situation, explain in your own words.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: When people share a task, the work becomes easier and faster.
   Working / marking points: One mark for sharing work and one for easier work.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Give food and clean water, provide a shelter, take it to a veterinary doctor when sick, do not overload it.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each way.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: day and play
   Working / marking points: One mark for each word.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Headline, lead, details, quote (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.
